Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch: feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches (commits 9f46912, ab04241 landed for Steps 1-2; Step 3's changes uncommitted — do not commit, do not stage, though you may read/investigate freely). Build mode. This is SFCC-91 Step 3 of 4: a new molecule, `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/` (4 new files) plus a 2-line registration edit to `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.

## Orchestrator's verdict (already run)

**IN SCOPE.** Exactly the 4 planned files, `theme/components/index.ts` diff confirmed exactly 2 insertions (Step 2's `ZimmColourSwatch` entry left as untouched context). All 5 hard-stop paths (`product-view/index.tsx`, the Step 2 atom, `swatch-group/`, translations, `theme/foundation/**`) verified with zero working-tree diff. No data-fetching hook in the new component. No consumer of `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` exists outside its own folder + the one registration (no premature Step 4 coupling).

## Tester's findings (already run — extremely thorough; built real render probes rather than reasoning about behaviour)

**🔴 CONFIRMED must-fix, empirically reproduced (not just traced):** the component renders a "Colour: {name}" label and, above 4 populated colours, a fixed 4-wide paginated window with prev/next chevrons. `const [pageStart, setPageStart] = useState(0)` always initializes to 0 regardless of where `selectedValue` actually sits in the `populated` array. Tester built a real test — 6 populated colours, `selectedValue` = the 6th (which sits on page 2) — and the actual rendered output on initial mount was:
```
rendered radio count: 4  (items 0-3, NOT the page containing the real selection)
checked count: 0         (nothing shows as selected anywhere on screen)
tabbable (tabindex=0) count: 0   (the entire visible radiogroup is untabbable via keyboard)
```
Root cause traced against base SFCC (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group/index.jsx:113`): base's `isFocusable = value ? selected : index === 0` is computed over ALL children since base never windows its render. This component's algebraically-identical formula (`isSelected || (!selectedValue && index === 0)`) is a faithful port, but applying it over a `windowed` slice is a precondition break — windowing can exclude the selected item entirely, which never happens in base. Tester confirmed the bug is isolated to the initial `pageStart` value, not a deeper logic error: manually paging to the correct page immediately recovers correct behaviour (`checked: ["Colour Six"], tabbable: ["Colour Six"]`). This is an unambiguous WCAG 2.2 AA keyboard-operability violation (AGENTS.md Accessibility section) — a shopper with a genuine, valid colour selection would see a swatch group where nothing appears selected AND cannot Tab into the swatch row at all, if that selection happens to sit beyond the 4th position. Tester also confirmed no existing story/test can ever catch this — the `Paginated` story's `selectedValue` (index 1) sits on page 1, so the scenario is structurally never exercised by anything shipped in this step.

**🟡 CONFIRMED should-fix — a fabricated citation, independently re-verified by me (the orchestrating session), not just Tester.** `index.tsx:156`'s comment reads: *"...is expressed as direct Chakra props with var(--zimm-*) values instead, per overrideStyling.md's 'your call' allowance for this one sub-piece."* I grepped `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` and every other `.md` file in the repo for the phrase "your call" myself, directly — it appears nowhere except this one comment. **Provenance, so this isn't misread as the implementer inventing something from nothing:** my own launch instructions for this step used the phrase "your call" when giving the implementer latitude on how to structure the label-group wrapper's layout. The implementer took that permission and, when writing the persisted code comment, mis-dressed it as a citation to a formal rule in `overrideStyling.md` that does not exist there. The outcome is the same either way: a future reader (or another agent, or CodeRabbit) would go looking for this "allowance" in the cited doc and not find it. On the underlying merits — is a dedicated recipe part actually required for that wrapper — Tester judged the actual values used (`var(--zimm-scale-2xs)`, `flex`, `minWidth`) are token-compliant regardless, and that the "one canonical styling surface" rule is scoped to interactive components with competing definitions, which doesn't obviously apply to a static one-off layout wrapper. So the structural choice may be defensible; the false citation is the actual defect.

**🟡 CONFIRMED should-fix — no regression coverage for the Figma-mandated truncation behaviour.** ("If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation" — an explicit interaction annotation on the source Figma node.) Tester proved truncation IS genuinely implemented (built a throwaway probe rendering an 80-character name, read real computed styles: `overflow:hidden; textOverflow:ellipsis; whiteSpace:nowrap` on the dynamic name span, confirmed absent on the static "Colour:" span) — so today's behaviour is correct — but zero test or story in the actual deliverable exercises a long name, so nothing guards this from regressing.

**Everything else Tester confirmed clean, independently, with real mutation/removal tests, not just reading:** AC 5 filter keyed only on `imageUrl` (neutered the real filter in the real file, watched 2 tests fail with real diffs, restored, confirmed byte-identical restoration, re-ran 8/8 green); AC 1 filter-then-count ordering; pagination mechanics (6→4+2 split, boundary at exactly 4 and exactly 5, disabled states at both ends, next-then-previous returns identical original set); selection persistence when paging away from and back to a visible selection; keyboard direction convention independently verified against base SFCC's own `DIRECTIONS` constant; the `ZimmIcon` Vitest mock is load-bearing (removed it, whole suite failed to collect with a real TypeError, restored); `recipeParts.test.ts` mechanically collected and passed a case named exactly `zimmColourSwatchGroup`; zero raw hex/px/rem/em outside comments; zero Chakra responsive-array shorthand; zero data-fetching hook; both sibling imports (`ZimmColourSwatch`, `ZimmIcon`) via relative paths per the established convention; theme registration confirmed exactly 2 lines.

**What Tester could not verify:** did not execute the literal Storybook `play` functions (no `test-storybook` script wired, judged a full Storybook build disproportionate) — substituted equivalent Vitest render+interaction probes covering the same scenarios, not identical to the real Storybook runner. jsdom doesn't resolve `var(--zimm-*)` to concrete pixel/hex values, so only token-reference correctness was confirmed, not final rendered pixels. No live axe-core/screen-reader run this round (Step 2's Tester did one on the atom; this round only checked DOM-level ARIA attributes via Testing Library). No sub-agent dispatch was available in Tester's environment — it worked every angle itself sequentially and disclosed this rather than presenting it as parallel coverage.

## Your job

Score against your six axes and return PASS or REWORK. This is structurally similar to Step 2's rework (a real defect that passed every automated gate and even the shipped test/story suite, surfaced only by deliberately constructing the one scenario nothing else exercised) — walk through what Correctness and Completeness should conclude given a WCAG 2.2 AA keyboard-operability violation that is empirically reproduced, not hypothetical. If REWORK, give the specific instruction for the next Implementer round: what state initialization needs to change (which page `pageStart` should derive from on mount/prop change, in terms of `selectedValue`'s position within `populated`), whether the fabricated citation needs correcting in the same round or can wait, and whether the missing truncation test coverage is this-round or can be deferred/logged. Also state whether a new story/test scenario (selection beyond the first page) should be REQUIRED as part of the fix, given Tester's finding that nothing currently shipped could ever catch a regression of this exact defect.

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Recipe for the PDP colour-swatch group — the "Colour: Bay Blue" label row, and (when there is
5	 * more than one populated colour) the row of ZimmColourSwatch rectangles beneath it. This recipe
6	 * only lays the group out; each swatch's own fill/border/focus styling stays in the sibling
7	 * ZimmColourSwatch atom's own recipe.
8	 *
9	 * Values below are read directly off Figma for this exact component, not estimated — node
10	 * 40000307:13867 ("ColourOptions"), within Zimmermann_Design_System_2026.
11	 *
12	 * Six parts:
13	 *   - `root` — outer vertical flex container: the label row above, the swatches row below.
14	 *   - `label` — the label row ("labelContainer" in Figma): the label-group (the two
15	 *     "Colour:"/name text pieces — laid out via a plain Chakra-prop wrapper in the component
16	 *     itself, not a seventh part here; see index.tsx's own comment for why) plus the pagination
17	 *     controls, right-aligned purely via the label-group's own `flex: 1 0 0` rather than an
18	 *     absolute-position hack.
19	 *   - `labelName` — the dynamic colour-name text specifically (e.g. "Bay Blue"). Gets its own
20	 *     part, unlike the static "Colour:" piece beside it, because it alone carries the
21	 *     Figma-mandated truncation behaviour: "If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation"
22	 *     (this node's own interaction annotation).
23	 *   - `swatches` — the horizontal row of rendered ZimmColourSwatch children.
24	 *   - `pagination` — wrapper around the two chevron buttons.
25	 *   - `pageButton` — each individual chevron button (24x24, holding a 16px ZimmIcon).
26	 */
27	export const ZimmColourSwatchGroup = {
28	  parts: ['root', 'label', 'labelName', 'swatches', 'pagination', 'pageButton'],
29	
30	  baseStyle: {
31	    root: {
32	      display: 'flex',
33	      flexDirection: 'column',
34	      // 8px between the label row and the swatches row. No background here — background lives
35	      // per-swatch, already handled by the atom's own recipe.
36	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
37	    },
38	
39	    label: {
40	      display: 'flex',
41	      alignItems: 'center',
42	      // 24px. Matches spacing.xl exactly, so the named step is used rather than the numerically
43	      // identical --zimm-scale-600 alias — see bottomBar.css.ts's own `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`
44	      // usage for the same 24px value elsewhere in this codebase.
45	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
46	      // 8px between the label-group and the pagination controls.
47	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
48	    },
49	
50	    labelName: {
51	      textStyle: 'caption',
52	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
53	      // The truncating half of the label-group's two text pieces (the static "Colour:" text
54	      // beside it never truncates — see index.tsx). `flex: 1 0 0` lets it consume the
55	      // label-group's remaining width; `minWidth: 0` is required for a flex item to actually
56	      // shrink below its content size instead of overflowing; the rest is the standard
57	      // single-line-ellipsis triad.
58	      flex: '1 0 0',
59	      minWidth: 0,
60	      overflow: 'hidden',
61	      textOverflow: 'ellipsis',
62	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
63	    },
64	
65	    swatches: {
66	      display: 'flex',
67	      width: '100%',
68	      // Confirmed directly off the Figma export, not a stylistic default: the 4-swatch example
69	      // measures exactly 192px total width for four 48px-wide swatches (4 x 48, no gap
70	      // contribution) — swatches sit directly adjacent. Do not add a gap here; that would be a
71	      // real deviation from the design, not a stylistic default.
72	      gap: 0,
73	    },
74	
75	    pagination: {
76	      display: 'flex',
77	      alignItems: 'center',
78	      // No inter-button gap value exists in the Figma export handed to this step — left at the
79	      // flex default (no `gap` declared at all) rather than invented. Revisit if a designer
80	      // confirms a real value.
81	    },
82	
83	    pageButton: {
84	      display: 'flex',
85	      alignItems: 'center',
86	      justifyContent: 'center',
87	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
88	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
89	      // Resets the native <button> UA chrome so the box is exactly the 24x24 the design calls
90	      // for, with the 16px ZimmIcon centred inside it by the flex alignment above.
91	      padding: 0,
92	      border: 'none',
93	      background: 'none',
94	      cursor: 'pointer',
95	      // No confirmed Figma spec for a disabled visual treatment on this control — same "leave an
96	      // unspecified visual state alone rather than invent one" precedent as swatch-group's own
97	      // disabled colour logic (see this codebase's Known Gaps notes). The native `disabled`
98	      // attribute (set in index.tsx) already makes the control genuinely inert and announces as
99	      // disabled to assistive tech; only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX
100	      // keyword, not a design token.
101	      _disabled: {
102	        cursor: 'not-allowed',
103	      },
104	      // Same uniform ring every other interactive control in ui-kits/ uses (zimmColourSwatch,
105	      // zimmNavItem) — --zimm-focus-ring already composites the border-width/colour pair.
106	      _focusVisible: {
107	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
108	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
109	      },
110	    },
111	  } satisfies Record<string, SystemStyleObject>,
112	};

## Independent verification performed

Before scoring, I read all four new files and the theme-registration diff directly, then independently re-derived and re-executed the two most load-bearing claims rather than taking the transcript on trust:

- **`npx tsc --noEmit`** — clean, zero output.
- **Shipped suite** (`npx vitest run .../index.test.tsx`) — 8/8 green, confirmed directly.
- **`recipeGuards.test.ts`** — 6/6 green (no bare-token-key violations anywhere, including this recipe).
- **`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`** — zero findings under `zimmColourSwatchGroup/` (the 13 flagged lines are all pre-existing, unrelated files).
- **The pagination/keyboard defect** — I wrote my own throwaway repro test (`__reviewer_repro.test.tsx`, 6 populated colours, `selectedValue` = the 6th), ran it live, captured real output, then deleted it and confirmed via `git status`/directory listing that the working tree returned to exactly the 4 original untracked files with zero residue. Actual output:
  ```
  REPRO rendered radio count: 4
  REPRO rendered names: [ 'Colour One', 'Colour Two', 'Colour Three', 'Colour Four' ]
  REPRO checked count: 0
  REPRO tabbable count: 0
  ```
  This matches Tester's finding exactly, from a scenario I constructed myself, independently of Tester's fixtures.
- **The fabricated citation** — grepped `.claude/rules/`, `AGENTS.md`, `.docs/` for the literal phrase "your call" myself: zero matches anywhere. Also read `overrideStyling.md` in full (available in context) and confirmed no such allowance exists there.
- **Base SFCC comparison** — read `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group/index.jsx` directly. Confirmed `isFocusable: value ? selected : index === 0` (line 113) is applied over `Children.toArray(children)` (all children, unwindowed), and that base's `selected`/`isFocusable` are derived fresh from the `value` prop on every render — its own mount-only `useEffect(..., [])` on `selectedIndex` is cosmetic there (only affects arrow-key bookkeeping), never gates what's rendered. This is why the override's structurally-identical formula, applied to a `.slice()`'d window, is a precondition break rather than a faithful port — confirmed by reading the base source myself, not by relying on Tester's characterization of it.

## Per-axis table (most severe first)

| Axis | Verdict | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| **Correctness** | **FAIL** | 🔴 Tester finding, independently reproduced live by me. `index.tsx:100`'s `useState(0)` never derives from `selectedValue`'s position — a real, shipped WCAG 2.2 AA keyboard-operability violation (SC 2.1.1, carried into 2.2), not a hypothetical edge case. |
| **Pass criteria** | **FAIL** | The component's own JSDoc (`index.tsx:90–92`) asserts "a selected colour that pages out of view stays selected" — but for a selection that starts beyond page 1, it is never rendered as selected or reachable at all. The documented contract is not met for a realistic input shape (any product with 5+ colourways where the referred/deep-linked colour isn't in the first four). |
| **Completeness** | **FAIL** | Two gaps, both confirmed by direct reading: (1) no test/story anywhere exercises a selection beyond the first page — `Paginated`'s fixture (`selectedValue: IVORY.value`, index 1) structurally sits on page 1, confirmed from the story source; (2) no test/story exercises the Figma-mandated truncation behaviour, despite it being correctly implemented. |
| **Conformance** | **FAIL** | `index.tsx:156`'s comment cites "overrideStyling.md's 'your call' allowance" — confirmed by my own grep across the whole rules/docs tree, this rule does not exist. A persisted, false citation to project documentation is exactly the kind of self-documentation-integrity issue this codebase's own Doc Integrity rule cares about. Everything else under this axis (styling hierarchy, `var(--zimm-*)` usage, relative sibling imports, namespacing, recipe registration) is independently confirmed clean. |
| **Design fidelity** | **UNVERIFIED** | The recipe cites real Figma node values (node `40000307:13867`, specific pixel measurements), which is stronger-than-usual traceability, but nothing in this review or Tester's disclosed work constitutes an actual rendered/visual checkpoint against that Figma node — no screenshot comparison, no live browser render. Per the house rule, this stays UNVERIFIED rather than PASS until that checkpoint happens. |
| **Restraint** | **PASS** | Orchestrator's verdict is IN SCOPE (exactly the 4 planned files + confirmed 2-line registration diff, all 5 hard-stop paths clean). I independently confirmed via `git status` that only those files are touched. Per the rule, Restraint takes its evidence from the Orchestrator's verdict, and it holds. |

## Overall: REWORK

## What I tried to falsify

- Attempted to find an escape hatch elsewhere in the tree that could make the mount-time bug moot (e.g. a `key`-based remount, an `initialPageStart` prop, or a wrapping effect in `product-view/index.tsx`). Confirmed none exists: `product-view/index.tsx` has zero working-tree diff, and `ZimmColourSwatchGroupProps` (lines 62–74) exposes only `label`/`selectedName`/`selectedValue`/`values` — no override point. The defect is fully contained and unmitigated.
- Tried to read the JSDoc's "stays selected... just not visible until paged back into view" claim (lines 90–92) as already covering the mount-time case, to see if this was working-as-documented rather than a real gap. It doesn't cover it — that clause describes interactively paging *away* from a visible selection, not the component's behaviour on first render with an already-distant selection.
- Checked the boundary the fix must not disturb: re-ran the shipped 8-test suite and `recipeGuards.test.ts` to confirm the existing green baseline is real (not a stale run), so the next round's diff can be judged against a known-good starting point.
- Tried to independently corroborate rather than restate every other Tester claim I could cheaply check myself: `tsc --noEmit`, the token audit script, and a full read of both `index.test.tsx` and `index.stories.tsx` for the two named coverage gaps. All independently confirmed.
- Looked for a reason the fabricated citation might be defensible on the merits regardless of the false citation (i.e., is the underlying structural choice itself wrong) — it isn't; the wrapper's actual values are token-compliant and the "one canonical styling surface" rule is plausibly scoped away from a static wrapper, so the defect is narrowly the false citation, not the code it's attached to.

## What I could not verify

- **Live Storybook `play` execution** and **axe-core/screen-reader pass** — not run this round (matches Tester's own disclosed limitation); DOM-level ARIA attributes only.
- **Rendered pixel/visual fidelity against the Figma node** — no screenshot or live-browser comparison was available to me either; Design fidelity is UNVERIFIED, not passed, for this reason.
- **Behaviour when `selectedValue` changes on an already-mounted instance** (as opposed to at mount) — no consumer of this component exists yet outside its own folder (Step 4 hasn't landed), so there is no live scenario to test this against today. I've included it as a required part of the fix anyway (see below) because the fix is cheap either way and the alternative is knowingly shipping the same bug shape a second time.

## Defects requiring fix

**1. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:100`** (declaration) and **:197–213** (render consequence) — **Blocker, CONFIRMED** (independently reproduced live, see above).

Instruction for the next Implementer round:
- Compute `selectedIndex = populated.findIndex((value) => value.value === selectedValue)`, then derive the page containing it: `Math.floor(selectedIndex / SWATCHES_PER_PAGE) * SWATCHES_PER_PAGE`, falling back to `0` when `selectedIndex === -1` — the same fallback convention already used for `isFocusable`'s `!selectedValue && index === 0` branch.
- This must hold both at initial mount *and* whenever `selectedValue` changes while the instance stays mounted — a lazy `useState(() => …)` initializer alone only fixes the former. Base SFCC's mount-only `useEffect(..., [])` is not a safe precedent to copy: in base, `selected`/`isFocusable` are derived fresh from the `value` prop every render regardless of that effect, so staleness there is harmless; here `pageStart` gates which items are even rendered, so staleness is directly observable as "nothing is selectable." Pair the initializer with a resync (e.g. a `useEffect` keyed on `selectedValue`/`populated`, or compute the default page fresh each render and let local state only override it after an explicit prev/next click) so a future Step-4-driven prop change doesn't resurrect this exact bug.
- **Required this round:** a Vitest test in `index.test.tsx` with >4 populated colours and `selectedValue` pointing beyond the first page, asserting on initial render (no interaction) that exactly one radio is `aria-checked="true"` and exactly one is `tabindex="0"`, both the actual selection. This belongs in this file per its own header's stated scope ("the roving-tabindex invariant that this component alone is responsible for proving").
- **Recommended, same round:** a sibling Storybook story to `Paginated` with the selection starting on page 2, asserting the same on-mount state before any click — cheap given the existing harness, and closes the exact visibility gap Tester named.

**2. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:156`** — **Should-fix, CONFIRMED** (grepped myself, zero matches for "your call" anywhere in `.claude/rules/`, `AGENTS.md`, `.docs/`).

Instruction: correct the comment to stop citing a nonexistent `overrideStyling.md` rule. State plainly that this is a structural choice made with the Orchestrator's latitude for this one sub-piece, not a documented allowance — e.g., note that it's a static non-interactive wrapper, so "one canonical styling surface per component type" (which is scoped to components with competing/interactive definitions) doesn't obviously require a dedicated recipe part here. Fix in the same round as Defect 1 — one line, zero design risk, no reason to burn a separate cycle on it.

**3. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx` / `index.stories.tsx`** (absence) — **Should-fix, CONFIRMED** (read both files in full; neither exercises a long colour name).

Instruction: add a Vitest test rendering a long `selectedName` (60+ chars) and asserting the truncation triad (`overflow:hidden; textOverflow:ellipsis; whiteSpace:nowrap`) on the dynamic name span and its absence on the static "Colour:" span. Fix in this round — fixtures/harness already exist, cost is low, and a named-but-deferred gap in this codebase has a track record of lingering (see the `overrideStyling.md` "Known gaps" section).

## Round tracking

This is Round 1 of the REWORK loop for Step 3 as presented to me — no prior round for this step is referenced. Flagging the round cap for awareness: if the next round fixes Defect 1 but reintroduces the same bug shape via a mount-only fix (see the prop-change caveat above), that would count toward the third-round stop condition, since it would be the same underlying defect recurring rather than a new one.
